newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Dollar could rise to 2.0 marks on weak EMU-Siebert.
newsitem.headline: Dollar could rise to 2.0 marks on weak EMU-Siebert.

text.p: The mark could conceivably fall to two marks to the dollar if a broad-based Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) undermines confidence in Europe's single currency, German economist Horst Siebert said.

"(With) a monetary union 15 minus 'X' (members), the euro will probably be weak, inflation will rise in Europe, we will have financial instability in world currency markets and political disputes on the dollar-euro exchange rate," he told the World Economic Forum.
Europe could have internal adjustment problems because of its inflexible labour markets and lack of political union, a scenario that would weaken the mark, he said.
"Since we have tremendous assets in marks around the world, 1.2 trillion marks in assets in German banks held by foreigners, this adjustment will have an impact on the exchange rate.
"I would not be surprised to see further devaluation of the D-mark to 1.80, 1.90 even conceivably to two marks to the dollar," he told a panel discussion.
